newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian party rejects president's talk offer.
newsitem.headline: Algerian party rejects president's talk offer.

text.p: Algeria's secular Socialist Forces Front (FFS) party said on Friday it had rejected President Liamine Zeroual's invitation to join talks on a general election promised by July this year.

The party, which came second to Islamist fundamentalists in the first round of an election cancelled in 1992, cited increased violence as a major reason. About 60,000 people have been killed in fighting since 1992, and authorities blame most of the deaths on Moslem rebels.

There has been an upsurge of killings during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan. Security forces and Algerian newspapers have reported about 300 people being killed since Ramadan started on January 10.

The FFS said in the statement sent to Reuters that Zeroual's invitation came at a time marked by "a terrible relaunch of terror, orgies of throat-cutting, bombs and carbombs which each week take hundreds of victims, men, women and children."
The FFS also accused the authorities of having already decided how the elections would be run and it refused to go along with a "prefabricated consensus".
"For the FFS, the choice is not between taking part or not in the elections, but between war and peace," it said.
Zeroual invited legal opposition parties for talks starting on February 11 to discuss the election, which the authorities see as a way to end the five-year-old crisis. Radical Islamists are excluded.

Algeria has had no elected parliament since January 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election dominated by the Islamist Salvation Front (FIS). The FIS was outlawed as violence followed the cancellation.

The FFS said that in Algeria there was a clamp on politics and the media to stifle the forces of peace and democracy and that a political solution or peace initiative to end the violence had been rejected.
